## E604 (2026-10-24): all isolation times under perturbation: what the record already holds, and an exhaustive check of the class windows
**Map:** owner (2026-10-24): "When we petrubed ap runners, did we watch all isolation times and how they moved or did not move? Did the isolation time get moved forward in back in time in a predictable way?" AP unit 1, speeds 1..8; the AP lonely instants of an end subject are c/8, c odd (E567).
**What the record already holds (searched: `RUNNING_LOG_order8_v1.md` E178 to E183 and E567, `MECHANISM_MAP_v5.md` R7):** E178 followed the cascade's first isolation along the deformation from the AP exactly (events located by exact bisection; 16,881 events on three populations: every event a pinch; at the AP start the class-1 window at 1/8 dies at once and the isolation moves to class 3 or class 5; jumps in R up to 1.4, 3.2 and 1.5, and negative jumps where a death and a birth coincide with the new window at 3/5 of the dying instant). E182: at a death the relocation is one of three cases (the partner's exit T_b; a window born earlier at the same instant; a later instant after a restart), in every simple death sampled; the restarted cascade stops no later than the reflected window. E567 (item 2) gives the deformation window of each class, class 1 as [1/(8 x_1), 7/(8 x_7)]. The statement in the owner's question is therefore answered in the record for the FIRST isolation along the path, event by event, on samples. This session's E597 to E603 recorded only the first isolation T per configuration (E603 followed one component per representative).
**Prediction [derived]:** at c/8, reading j with j c = 1 (mod 8) has its zone exit exactly there, reading j with j c = 7 (mod 8) has its zone entry exactly there. After a perturbation with readings x_j the instant becomes the interval [L(c), R(c)], L(c) = max over j with j c = 1 (mod 8) of (j c/8)/x_j and R(c) = min over j with j c = 7 (mod 8) of (j c/8)/x_j, alive iff L <= R.
**Script:** `experiments/n8/all_isolation_times_v1.py`: every runner offset in {-1/1000, 0, +1/1000} (3^8 = 6,561 patterns, exhaustive), every subject, every odd c in 1..15 (two periods); exact lonely intervals (complement of the union of open zones; touching zones leave a point).
**Result [OBS, exact, exhaustive]:** END subjects (runner 1 and runner 8), 104,976 (pattern, subject, c) cases: 58,320 predicted alive, in all of them the actual lonely interval near c/8 equals [L, R] exactly; 46,656 predicted dead, in all of them no lonely instant near c/8; zero mismatches. Direction among the alive cases: left edge earlier than c/8 in 25,272, later in 9,720, at c/8 in 23,328; right edge later in 25,272, earlier in 9,720, at c/8 in 23,328. The edge of tight reading j is at (j c/8)/x_j, so it moves earlier when x_j is larger than j and later when smaller. INTERIOR subjects: their AP lonely set is not isolated points (reading 7 is absent, so some c have no right-tight reading and the interval is bounded by non-tight readings); the prediction as stated does not apply to them and 314,928 interior cases are not analysed here.
**An error found on the way:** the first interval code merged touching zones and so deleted lonely instants of zero width; fixed (merge only on strict overlap). `classC_path_v1.py` (E603) has the same merge; its 'born' and 'deformed' labels for the representatives are to be rechecked (the landing switches and walls of `classC_walls_v1.py` use the cascade directly and are not affected).
**Consequence (M7):** the whole lonely set of the perturbed AP is predicted exactly by the tight readings for end subjects at first order, for the eight classes c = 1..15; the first isolation along the whole deformation was followed in E178 to E183. The step the record still lacks is the interior subjects' lonely set and the large-deviation chambers.

## E605 (2026-10-24): the wall list and the chamber-constancy test
**Map:** owner (2026-10-24): "Yes, enumerate every wall (a,b) between the AP readings with its distance from the AP ratio, and the chamber each bounds, for end and interior subjects, exact, and test that the cascade landing is constant on each chamber." E603 (pairwise walls), E567/E575.
**Walls [derived, exact]:** zone of reading x at lap n is the open interval ((n-1/8)/x, (n+1/8)/x). The cascade compares only zone edges of two readings, so the walls are: pinch exit(A,nA) = entry(B,nB), ratio x_A/x_B = (8nA+1)/(8nB-1) (nA >= 0, nB >= 1); exit tie exit(A,nA) = exit(B,nB), ratio (8nA+1)/(8nB+1) (nA, nB >= 0). A wall w between AP readings p, q is reachable at reading deviation eps iff w lies in [(p-eps)/(q+eps), (p+eps)/(q-eps)]; the least eps is |w q - p|/(1+w) (exact). File `experiments/n8/wall_list_v1.txt` (2,920 lines): for the four subject types k = 0,1,2,3 (AP readings [1,..,7], [1,1,2,..,6], [1,1,2,2,3,4,5], [1,1,2,2,3,3,4]; k and 7-k are mirror images) the walls with instant t* = (8nA+1)/(8 p_A) at most 7/8 at deviation bound 1/4 (89, 59, 43, 32 walls) and at most 3/2 at bound 1/2 (812, 690, 608, 575 walls), each with wall value, AP ratio, eps_min and t*. Walls with eps_min = 0 (tight at the AP): 4 for k=0 (ratios 1/7, 3/5, 5/3, 7), 2 for k=1, 2 for k=2, none for k=3. The nearest walls that are not tight at the AP for k=0 (deviation bound 1/4): 25/31 (AP 4/5; eps_min 1/56), 41/7 (AP 6; 1/48), 9/31 (AP 2/7; 1/40), 17/23 (AP 3/4; 1/40), 25/7 (AP 7/2; 1/32).
**Chamber test [OBS, exact, exhaustive on the E601 grid]:** `experiments/n8/walls_chambers_v1.py`: for each subject type a chamber is a cell of the sign vector of the reachable walls over the sorted readings; all 5^8 = 390,625 offset vectors of the grid (rho = 1/8, reading deviation bound 1/4); the entire cascade path (sorted index of the setter and its lap at every step) is compared inside each cell. Results: k=0 with walls up to t* <= 7/8: 89 walls, 73,530 chambers realised, 52,280 holding at least 2 configurations (369,375 of 390,625 cases), 0 path violations; with walls up to 1/2, 5/8, 3/4: 847, 448, 26 violations, so the walls with t* in (3/4, 7/8] are needed. k=1,2,3 with t* <= 7/8: 0 violations (13,723, 3,540, 920 chambers). At rho = 1/4 (deviation bound 1/2): with t* <= 7/8, k = 0,1,2 have 0 violations and k = 3 has 26; with t* <= 3/2 all four have 0 violations; at rho = 1/4 most cells hold one configuration (for k=0 with t* <= 3/2: 58,975 cells with at least 2 configurations holding 124,512 of 390,625 cases), so the test there is weak.
**Not done [PARTIAL]:** the grid has 5 values per runner, not every real deviation; the walls are enumerated, not each chamber's polytope or its landing formula; radii beyond 1/4; the constancy of the landing T value within a chamber is not the claim (T varies continuously inside a chamber; the path is what is constant).
**Consequence (M7) [OBS, PARTIAL]:** on this grid the cascade path is a function of the sign pattern of the walls with instants up to 7/8 (the last AP lonely instant of the first period) at radius 1/8, for the four subject types; that is an observation about this grid, not a landing formula and not a statement about every real deviation.
**Audit:** `rules-auditor` on the first drafts of E604 and E605 found two breaches (rule 13, a claim about the record without a search; rule 18, "complete" on a partial result); corrected above after reading E178 to E183 and E567.

## E606 (2026-10-24): the whole lonely set of every subject under small perturbation, end and interior; what the record already holds
**Map:** owner (2026-10-24): "Analyse those then" (the 314,928 interior cases left unanalysed in E604) and "Yes after you do a search in the corpus to make sure you are not relitigating prior work". E604, E567, E178 to E183.
**Corpus search (full text, scope stated):** (1) every `docs/n8/*.md` (the only other files under `docs/n8` are one .txt and one .out) for lines with "interior" near "lonely set", "window", "component", "interval" or "edge": the running log (21 lines) and `MANUSCRIPT_v23_4` to `MANUSCRIPT_v25_3` (3 lines each, the same three); also `MECHANISM_MAP_v5.md` for "interior subject", "interior runner", "interior_firstIso", "ap_interior", "lonely set", "clear set". (2) The Lean library in full text, all 3,108 `.lean` files under `LonelyRunner/LonelyRunner` and `LonelyRunnerFresh/Fresh`: the 10 files with "interior" within three lines of "lonely set", "window", "interval", "edge" or "component" were read at those lines (`DeformationN`, `GridPairLawN`, `LapDeadlineN`, `SymbolicWindowTransportN`, `IntLRC_5_Bienia`, `PathLaws`, `FiveReach`, `APNeighbourhood`, `Gate`, `Fresh/GridPairLaw`), and the headers of `WindowN`, `WindowPinchN`, `MaximalWindowTransportN`, `SymbolicWindowTransportN`, `IncomingWindowN`, `MovingCoreWindowsN`, `GridPairLawN` were read. Method limit: a text match on the word "interior", so a file about interior subjects that never uses the word would be missed.
**Found:** (a) log line 637 (early entry): the interior runners are not tight at the AP, the lonely set has interior. (b) E45 (log line 3758): interior runner: first isolation 1/(8d), d the nearer speed neighbour, every other reading in [d, 7d]. (c) E566 to E570 (`APLawR3_Interior`: `ap_interior_firstIso_max`, `ap_interior_lands_max`, speeds within 1/16; `APLawR4_All12`: all eight subjects within 1/12): first isolation. (d) `WindowPinchN.intervals_iff_max_le_min`: a finite family of closed intervals intersects iff max lower <= min upper; `WindowPinchN` states exact lap windows and the first pinch along an AP deformation with affine slacks; `SymbolicWindowTransportN` (`pinch_interior`, `slack_at_pinch`) and `MaximalWindowTransportN.rational_first_loss`: the first loss of a fixed lap vector along the deformation is at a rational parameter. (e) `GridPairLawN` (manuscript v25.3 section 4.3: `opening_at_u`, `entry_at_w`, `u_le_w_iff`, `grid_interval_lonely`, `grid_pair_law`): for a grid with a complete nonzero residue system, the class-a interval [u_a, w_a], u_a = o_A a/(8 d_A) (the opener's zone exit), w_a = o_B a/(8 d_B) (the closer's zone entry), is lonely under a displacement hypothesis eta <= 1/8; `u_le_w_iff`: u_a <= w_a iff o_A d_B <= o_B d_A; this is `ProgressionPairN.pair_law` for any grid. (f) The other matches use "interior" for topological interior points of the lonely set (`PathLaws.interior_iff_strict`) or for interior READINGS with residue 2 to 6 (`interior_res`, `clear_interior`); none states the lonely intervals of an interior subject under perturbation.
**Consequence for E603 to E605:** the pairwise ratio walls found there are the pair-law conditions `u_le_w_iff` in this record (the pinch wall exit(A,nA) = entry(B,nB) is `(8 n_A+1) d_B = (8 n_B+7) d_A`, the entry lap being n_B + 1 in the E605 convention). The end-subject window [L, R] of E604 is `GridPairLawN`'s [u_a, w_a] for the AP. They are not new; what E603 to E605 add is the enumeration, the exact distances from the AP ratios, and the checks on grids. Not found by this search: the whole lonely set of an INTERIOR subject under perturbation (a grid whose readings do not form a complete nonzero residue system, which `GridPairLawN`'s hypotheses exclude).
**Setting:** AP speeds 1, 2, ..., 8 (unit 1); every runner has a positive speed and the subject is one of the eight, with its own speed and its own offset; a reading is the difference of two positive speeds; no runner is stationary. Runners are named by their AP speed. For the subject with AP speed s, the readings are p = |s' - s| for the seven other AP speeds s', so p >= 1 (the scripts index the subject by k = s - 1). The end subjects are the runners with AP speeds 1 and 8; the interior subjects those with AP speeds 2 to 7. Zone of a runner with reading p at lap n: the open interval ((n-1/8)/p, (n+1/8)/p).
**Prediction [derived, an instance of the fixed-lap window criterion (d)]:** the AP lonely set of a subject in (0, T] is the union of components [a,b] = the gaps between the merged zones (a point for end subjects; intervals, with some points, for interior subjects). For a component let E_a = the zone exits exactly at a and B_b = the zone entries exactly at b. After a small perturbation with readings x the component becomes [L, R], L = max over E_a of (n+1/8)/x, R = min over B_b of (n-1/8)/x; alive iff L <= R.
**AP structure [exact]** (`lonely_set_all_subjects_v1.py structure`; script index k = s - 1): first period (instants up to 1): AP speeds 1 and 8: the four points 1/8, 3/8, 5/8, 7/8. AP speeds 2 and 7: [1/8, 7/48], [9/32, 7/24], the point 3/8, [17/40, 7/16], [9/16, 23/40], the point 5/8, [17/24, 23/32], [41/48, 7/8]. AP speeds 3 and 6: [1/8, 7/40], [9/32, 7/24], the point 3/8, [17/40, 7/16], [9/16, 23/40], the point 5/8, [17/24, 23/32], [33/40, 7/8]. AP speeds 4 and 5: [1/8, 7/32], [9/32, 7/24], [3/8, 7/16], [9/16, 5/8], [17/24, 23/32], [25/32, 7/8]. The smallest gap between AP components is 1/4 (end subjects) and 1/20 or 1/16 (interior).
**Test [OBS, exact; complete enumeration of a stated finite grid, not every real deviation]:** `experiments/n8/lonely_set_all_subjects_v1.py`: every runner offset in {-1/1000, 0, +1/1000} (3^8 = 6,561 patterns), all 8 subjects, every AP component with b <= 11/5 (a cutoff in time); the actual lonely set is the complement of the union of the open zones (touching zones leave a point). END subjects (118,098 component cases): 65,610 alive, in all of them the actual lonely interval equals [L, R] exactly; 52,488 dead, in all of them none near. INTERIOR subjects (603,612 component cases): 556,956 alive, equal to [L, R] exactly; 46,656 dead (the point components), none near. No mismatch in either; every component had both an exit at a and an entry at b. Movement of the interior intervals: width grows in 117,288 cases, shrinks in 325,944, unchanged in 55,404; left edge earlier in 129,276, later in 238,140, same in 189,540; right edge earlier in 230,364, later in 137,052, same in 189,540. The point components of interior subjects: width grows in 46,656 and stays unchanged in 11,664. Interval components never died at these perturbations.
**Not done:** perturbations larger than 1/1000 (the prediction concerns identified edges and fails once a new zone reaches a component or a birth occurs, E603); a Lean statement for interior subjects; a proof that the prediction holds for every small perturbation (three values per runner, not every real deviation); components later than t = 11/5.
**Consequence (M7) [OBS, on this grid]:** at first order the whole lonely set of every subject of the perturbed AP is the image of the AP's components under two explicit maps (the latest exit and the earliest entry among the readings bounding it); each edge moves earlier or later by the sign and size of the bounding reading's deviation, for end and interior subjects alike on this grid. For end subjects this is `GridPairLawN`; for interior subjects the check above is the only support found.
**Audit:** `rules-auditor` on three drafts: breaches on the first (rule 13, two files only), second (rule 14 "exhaustive", rule 13 Lean by name, rule 5 index 0) and none on the third; fixed as stated.

## E607 (2026-10-24): the first-order lonely window in Lean: general theorem and the interior subject's first component
**Map:** owner (2026-10-24): "state and prove in Lean (new file) the first-order lonely-set statement for a component with a left exit set and right entry set: for deviations small enough, the component becomes [max exits, min entries], and the interior-subject case follows." E606 (the exact tests), E604, `GridPairLawN`, `WindowPinchN.intervals_iff_max_le_min` (E606 corpus search).
**Lean [L], new file `LonelyRunnerFresh/Fresh/WindowFirstOrder.lean`** (axioms propext, choice, Quot.sound; sorry 0; untagged Props 0; builds with `./check.sh`):
- `zone_iff`, `lonely_iff_nozone`: a reading x is clear at t (1/8 <= distInt(x t)) iff t lies in no zone ((z - 1/8)/x, (z + 1/8)/x), z an integer.
- `edge_pert`, `zone_facts`: the zone edges move by at most 2|c| eps under |x - p| <= eps (p >= 1, eps <= 1/2), and the four consequences used below.
- **`window_iff`**: readings p i (AP) with 1 <= p i <= 7 and x i with |x i - p i| <= eps; an AP lonely component [a, b] with margin delta (0 < delta <= 1/28, delta < a), T >= b + delta, an integer Z0 >= 8T + 1, 8 (Z0 + 1) eps <= delta, and the AP classification hcls of every zone with laps 0..Z0: far left of the window (exit <= a - delta), far right (entry >= b + delta), exactly an exit at a, or exactly an entry at b. Conclusion: for t in [a - delta/2, b + delta/2], x is clear for every reading iff t >= (z + 1/8)/x i for every AP exit zone (z, i) at a and t <= (z - 1/8)/x i for every AP entry zone at b.
- **`window_iff_maxmin`**: with finite nonempty exit set EX and entry set EN (exactly the AP exit zones at a and entry zones at b): lonely for every reading iff max over EX of (z + 1/8)/x <= t <= min over EN of (z - 1/8)/x, in the window. This is the statement "the component becomes [max exits, min entries]" for small deviations.
- **Interior subject, AP speed 2** (`pInt2` = (1,1,2,3,4,5,6); component [1/8, 7/48]; delta = 1/56, T = 55/336, Z0 = 3): `pInt2_cls` (the classification of all 28 zones with laps 0..3, finite check, by interval_cases and fin_cases), `interior2_window` (readings form, eps <= 1/1792: lonely iff 1/(8 x_0) <= t, 1/(8 x_1) <= t, t <= 7/(8 x_6)), and **`interior2_arrangement`**: speeds v_i with |v_i - (i + 1)| <= eta, eta <= 1/3584, subject runner 1 (AP speed 2): in [1/8 - 1/112, 7/48 + 1/112], IsolatedAt v 1 t iff 1/(8 |v 0 - v 1|) <= t and 1/(8 |v 2 - v 1|) <= t and t <= 7/(8 |v 7 - v 1|), i.e. the component is [1/(8 d), 7/(8 r_6)] with d the nearer neighbour gap.
**Transcription check [OBS, exact]:** `experiments/n8/interior2_theorem_check_v1.py`: all 3^8 patterns of speeds i + 1 + {-1/3584, 0, 1/3584}, 61 grid times in the window and the predicted edges with offsets of 1/1000000: 439,587 cases, 0 disagreements between `IsolatedAt` and the three-inequality form.
**What this does not give:** (a) the other components of the interior subject and the other interior subjects: each needs its own finite classification check (the instance `pInt2_cls` is the model; E606 verified the prediction numerically for all of them at deviation 1/1000, not by proof); (b) the deviation bound of the theorem (eta <= 1/3584, eps <= 1/1792) is smaller than the 1/1000 of E606's test, so that test is not covered by this proof; (c) deviations beyond the bound, where a zone reaches the component or a lonely component is born (E603); (d) the end subjects' points (the case a = b) are an instance of `window_iff` with a = b but no instance was written; (e) the corpus has `GridPairLawN` for end subjects; this entry is not compared with its hypotheses beyond what E606 states.
**Consequence (M7):** the first-order statement "a lonely component becomes [max exits, min entries] under deviations below a margin-dependent bound" is a Lean theorem in general form (`window_iff_maxmin`), and one interior-subject component (the first of AP speed 2) is an instance with explicit constants, giving the explicit window [1/(8 d), 7/(8 r_6)] for the first lonely component of that subject. I did not find this localisation form (classification plus deviation bound gives exactly the max/min window) stated in the library in the E606 search.
**Audit:** `rules-auditor` on the draft: no breaches.

## E609 (2026-10-24): open exploratory analysis of the perturbation grid: what the data shows beyond the prediction
**Map:** owner (2026-10-24): "I think we should analyse the data more for all the pertubation test, you seem to have reviewed them against a prediction but not actually analysed them for any other pattern." Data: AP speeds 1..8 (unit 1), every runner offset in {-1/1000, 0, +1/1000} (3^8 = 6,561 patterns), all 8 subjects (runners named by AP speed s), exact Fractions; lonely set of each subject = complement of the union of open zones, components in (0, 11/5]. E604, E606, E608 for the setting. Scripts `experiments/n8/explore_patterns_v1.py`, `explore_patterns2_v1.py`, `explore_patterns3_v1.py`, `explore_global_v1.py`. No result below assumes the E606 prediction.
**All results are [OBS, exact, complete enumeration of this ternary grid at eps = 1/1000] unless stated.**
1. **Only relative offsets matter.** Adding the same offset to every runner leaves the whole lonely set unchanged: 4,096 of 4,096 shifted pairs. The subset size m of E608 is therefore not the natural organiser (m = 8 with equal signs is the identity; shifted patterns repeat); the natural variable is the offsets relative to the subject.
2. **Locality.** For each subject the smallest set of runners whose offsets determine the first-isolation class (A: T = 1/8; B: T = 1/(8 d_min); C: other) has 3 members, and it is unique: subject s = 2..7: runners {s-1, s, s+1} (the subject and its two neighbours); subject 1: {1, 2, 8}; subject 8: {1, 7, 8} (the end runners are each other's neighbours on the circle). The first-isolation instant T itself is determined by the same three runners for s = 2..7 and by five runners for the end subjects: {1, 2, 4, 6, 8} for s = 1 and {1, 3, 5, 7, 8} for s = 8 (the readings 3 and 5 enter). Determination here means a function of the offsets of those runners over this grid.
3. **Mirror symmetry** (runner i to runner 7-i, offsets negated, subject k to 7-k, indices 0-based): the whole lonely set is identical in 52,488 of 52,488 (pattern, subject) cases, and the first-isolation class in 52,488 of 52,488.
4. **Pair law, end subjects.** Of the AP instants 1/8, 7/8, 3/8, 5/8: in every one of the 13,122 end-subject cases at least one of {1/8, 7/8} is alive and at least one of {3/8, 5/8}; both of a pair are alive only at an exact tie (1,458 cases each, 1/9 of the cases); neither of a pair never occurs.
5. **Pair law, interior subjects with point components** (AP speeds 2, 3, 6, 7): for the pair {3/8, 5/8}, exactly one is alive in 5,832 of 6,561 patterns (2,916 each way), both in 729 (1/9, ties), neither in 0.
6. **Class rules (exact on every cell).** End subject 1, with d_i = s_i - s_1 the relative offsets: the class is a function of (d_2, d_8) alone, 19 cells all pure: d_2 >= 1: B; d_2 = 0: A if d_8 <= 0 and C if d_8 >= 1; d_2 <= -1: C. Interior subjects 2..7 with a = s_{s-1} - s_s, b = s_{s+1} - s_s (left gap 1 - a, right gap 1 + b): class A iff min(1 - a, 1 + b) = 1, else B, and class C never occurs; 19 cells per subject, all pure, 0 contradictions.
7. **Class C landings.** At eps = 1/1000 every class C first isolation equals (n + 1/8)/x for exactly two (reading rank, lap n): (3, 1) in 3,024 cases and (5, 3) in 2,808; all are end subjects; no interior case is class C.
8. **Which components can die.** All interval components of every interior subject (first period) are alive in every pattern. Only the point components can die, and the survival of each is determined by exactly three runners: subject 1: {1, 2, 8} for the points 1/8 and 7/8, {1, 4, 6} for 3/8 and 5/8; subject 8: {1, 7, 8} and {3, 5, 8}; subject 2: {2, 5, 7}; subject 3: {3, 6, 8}; subject 6: {1, 3, 6}; subject 7: {2, 4, 7} (the subject and the two runners at readings j and 8 - j). The subjects with AP speeds 4 and 5 have no point components and nothing dies.
9. **Total length is not conserved:** the change of the total length of the lonely set with left edge below 1, divided by eps, takes both signs for the interior subjects (it takes only values >= 0 for end subjects, whose AP length is 0).
10. **Global isolation.** An instant in (0, 1] at which all 8 subjects are lonely together exists in 3 of the 6,561 patterns (the AP and the two patterns that shift every runner equally, where it is exactly 1/8) and in none of the other 6,558, including every pattern with only one runner offset. Among those 6,558 the eight first isolations take 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 distinct values in 330, 1,560, 3,012, 1,528, 128 patterns.
**Not done:** deviations larger than 1/1000 for these questions (E608 shows the whole-set prediction fails from 1/16); the determining-set search covers subsets of runners by size and does not test sufficiency beyond this grid; interior-subject components of later periods; a Lean statement of any of these.
**Consequence (M7) [OBS, on this grid]:** at first order each runner's individual isolation (its first isolation class, and the survival of its point components) is a function of only three runners' relative offsets, so the individual isolations are local, and the global isolation is destroyed at once by any relative perturbation.
**Audit:** `rules-auditor` on the draft: no breaches.

## E610 (2026-10-24): the smallest deviation at which the whole-set prediction first fails, by subset size, and the wall that causes it (horizons 1 and 3/2)
**Map:** owner (2026-10-24): "find the smallest deviation at which the whole-set prediction first fails, by subset size, and classify the first birth or merge there in wall terms." E606 and E608 (the prediction: each AP lonely component [a,b] becomes [L,R], L the latest zone exit at a, R the earliest zone entry at b, alive iff L <= R), E603 and E605 (walls). AP speeds 1..8 (unit 1); every runner keeps a positive speed.
**Method:** for every subset S of the 8 runners (m = 1..8) and every sign pattern on S (6,560 patterns), every subject (52,480 cases): the ray v(eps) = AP + eps s. Readings are exactly x_i(eps) = p_i + eps sigma_i (p_i AP reading, sigma_i the relative offset). Failure at eps means the actual lonely components with right edge <= H differ from the predicted alive intervals with R <= H (comparing only components inside the horizon H on both sides removes the artifact of a component crossing the cutoff). Scan eps over the 65 values 1/1000 + j (1/16 - 1/1000)/64, j = 0..64, then bisect in exact rationals (40 steps) between the last passing and the first failing value, so the final bracket has the exact width (1/16 - 1/1000)/(64 * 2^40). Inside the final bracket the pairs of zone edges that could tie are found by a search window (edges closer than 1/10^9 at the upper end of the bracket; this window only steers the search): for each candidate pair the tie is solved exactly, edges c1/(p1 + eps sigma1) and c2/(p2 + eps sigma2) are equal at eps* = -(c2 p1 - c1 p2)/(c1 sigma2 - c2 sigma1), and the candidate is accepted only if this exact rational lies in the exact bracket. Script `experiments/n8/failure_threshold_v1.py` (HORIZON environment variable); raw results `failure_threshold_raw_m1_2_3_4_5_6_7_8_T1.pkl` and `_T3_2.pkl`; analysis `explore_failures_v1.py`, `check_eps_star_identity_v1.py`. Exact Fractions. All 6,560 patterns and 8 subjects were run [PARTIAL: eps only up to 1/16; failure intervals narrower than the scan spacing (1/16 - 1/1000)/64 would be missed]; no failure is found at eps = 1/1000 at either horizon (0 of 52,480).
**Result, horizon H = 1 [OBS, exact]:** failing in (1/1000, 1/16]: 24,904 of 52,480 cases; no failure up to 1/16: 27,576. Smallest eps* by subset size m = 1, 2, 3..8: 1/31, 1/56, 1/62 (the same 1/62 for every m from 3 to 8). The wall at the smallest eps* is the same for every m: the exit of the zone of the reading with p = 4 at lap 3 meets the entry of the zone of the reading with p = 5 at lap 4, ratio x_4/x_5 = 25/31 (AP ratio 4/5; the two edges are 1/160 = 1/(8 4 5) apart at the AP), at the instant t* = 25/32.
**Result, horizon H = 3/2 [OBS, exact]:** failing: 41,120 of 52,480; no failure up to 1/16: 11,360. Smallest eps* for m = 1, 2, 3..8: 1/81, 1/139, 1/162 (the same for every m from 3 to 8). The wall: the exit of the zone of the reading p = 7 at lap 10 meets the entry of the zone of the reading p = 2 at lap 3, ratio 81/23, at t* = 81/56.
**Classification of the first failure in wall terms [OBS, exact]:** H = 1: wall kinds over all walls found (31,350 in all; each failing case has at least one): entry-exit 25,444, entry-entry 3,390, exit-exit 2,516. Change in the number of components over the event, by the kind of the first wall (24,904 failing cases): entry-exit pinch with +1 component (a birth): 21,794; entry-exit with +2: 326; entry-exit with 0: 96; entry-entry with 0 (an edge handed to another zone): 1,634; exit-exit with 0: 1,050; entry-entry with +1: 4. H = 3/2 (41,120 failing cases): entry-exit +1: 30,166; exit-exit 0: 4,982; entry-entry 0: 4,782; entry-exit 0: 278; entry-exit -1 (a death): 222; exit-exit +1: 194; entry-entry +1: 194; entry-exit +2: 152; entry-entry -1: 96; exit-exit -1: 54. In 22,058 of the 31,350 walls at H = 1 and 35,132 of the 54,386 at H = 3/2 the AP near-miss integer D = 8 (c1 p2 - c2 p1) equals 1, the smallest possible gap 1/(8 p1 p2).
**Quantisation and invariances [OBS, exact]:** only 34 distinct values of eps* occur at H = 1 and 76 at H = 3/2; eps* is a function of the subject and the relative-offset vector alone (0 of 24,304 classes at H = 1, 0 of 40,034 at H = 3/2 have members that disagree).
**Derived identity [P], checked [OBS, exact]:** at the tie, writing t* for the common edge value at eps*, c1 sigma2 - c2 sigma1 = t* (p1 sigma2 - p2 sigma1) because the eps* terms cancel; hence eps* t* = |D| / (8 |p1 sigma2 - p2 sigma1|) exactly. It holds in all 31,350 walls at H = 1 and all 54,386 walls at H = 3/2, and the smallest eps* t* is 1/112 at both horizons (attained at H = 3/2 by the wall above: (1/162)(81/56) = 1/112). So the first-failure deviation falls like 1/t*: it is not a property of the AP alone but of the horizon, and for horizon H the observed values satisfy eps* >= 1/(112 H) (this bound is observed at these two horizons, not proved).
**Not done:** horizon 11/5 (running at the time of writing); deviations of unequal size; eps beyond 1/16 (the 27,576 and 11,360 cases without failure up to 1/16 are not followed further); a Lean statement of the identity.
**Consequence (M7) [OBS and P]:** under equal-size perturbations the whole-set prediction first fails by a wall tie of two zone edges, most often a pinch that gives birth to a new lonely component (21,794 of 24,904 failing cases at H = 1 and 30,166 of 41,120 at H = 3/2), at a deviation set exactly by the AP near-miss D, the two readings and the relative offsets; the smallest such deviation shrinks as the horizon grows (1/62 at H = 1, 1/162 at H = 3/2).
**Audit:** `rules-auditor` on three drafts: breaches on the first (rule 15, decimal tolerances and percentages) and second (rule 18, "complete" on a partial result); fixed as stated.

## E611 (2026-10-24): horizon 11/5 for the first-failure threshold (completes E610's three horizons)
**Map:** E610 (method, identity eps* t* = |D| / (8 |p1 sigma2 - p2 sigma1|)); same script `experiments/n8/failure_threshold_v1.py` with HORIZON = 11/5; raw results `failure_threshold_raw_m1_2_3_4_5_6_7_8_T11_5.pkl`.
**Result [OBS, exact]:** 52,480 cases; failing at 1/1000: 0; no failure up to 1/16: 5,246; failing in (1/1000, 1/16]: 47,234. Smallest eps* for m = 1, 2, 3..8: 1/87, 1/149, 1/174 (the same 1/174 for every m from 3 to 8, subject with AP speed 1, subset containing the runners with AP speeds 1, 3 and 8). Summary of the three horizons, smallest eps* for m = 1 / 2 / 3..8: H = 1: 1/31, 1/56, 1/62; H = 3/2: 1/81, 1/139, 1/162; H = 11/5: 1/87, 1/149, 1/174. Wall kinds over the walls found (70,712): entry-exit 39,950, exit-exit 18,036, entry-entry 12,726. AP near-miss integer D = 1 in 40,487 of the 70,712 walls. Distinct eps* values: 142. eps* is a function of the subject and the relative offsets alone (0 of 45,954 classes disagree). The identity eps* t* = |D| / (8 |p1 sigma2 - p2 sigma1|) holds exactly in all 70,712 walls, and the smallest eps* t* is again 1/112.
**The bound eps* >= 1/(112 H) of E610:** observed again, not attained at H = 11/5: the smallest eps* is 1/174 against 1/(112 H) = 5/1232; the walls with the product exactly 1/112 occur at particular instants (t* = 81/56 at H = 3/2 and t* = 87/56 here), so the smallest threshold does not keep falling in proportion to 1/H beyond those instants. It remains an observation on three horizons.
**442 failing cases with no tie-wall found, explained [OBS, exact]:** 442 of the 47,234 failing cases have no zone-edge tie in the bracket. All have the same bracket (around eps = 3/88) and the same change of +1 in the number of components. For each of the 442 an edge crosses exactly H = 11/5 at an exact rational eps inside the bracket (checked for all 442: the entry of the zone of the reading p = 4 at lap 9 equals H at eps = 3/88, x = 4 + 3/88 = 355/88). So these are horizon-entry events: a component whose left edge already differs from the prediction (the prediction failed earlier) becomes visible when its right edge crosses H, because failure is judged only on components with right edge <= H. They are not walls, and they do not change the smallest eps* (3/88 is above 1/174). A definition of failure that compares components by left edge would date their failure earlier; not done.
**Not done:** that re-definition; eps beyond 1/16; unequal-size perturbations.
**Consequence (M7) [OBS]:** the first-failure deviation by subset size is 1/87, 1/149, 1/174 at H = 11/5; the three horizons give smallest thresholds 1/62, 1/162, 1/174 for m >= 3.
**Audit:** `rules-auditor` on the draft: no breaches.

## E613 (2026-10-24): the locality, symmetry and pair-law findings of E609 in Lean [PARTIAL]
**Map:** owner (2026-10-24): "Can we please prove this in lean, they seem foundational." (the E609 findings: locality, mirror symmetry, pair laws, two landings, point-component survival).
**Corpus search (scope stated):** (1) Lean library, full text over all 3,108 `.lean` files under `LonelyRunner/LonelyRunner` and `LonelyRunnerFresh/Fresh`, for statements that isolation or first isolation is invariant under a uniform shift of speeds, a runner reflection, or unique: the docstring of `Fresh/Cycle.lean` states the principle that every isolation statement is about differences, and `Cycle.lean` has lemmas for changes between grids (`isolatedAt_gridShift_iff`, `isolatedAt_grid_iff`, `single_change_*`), which are statements about changing speeds from one grid to another; no standalone lemma that adding one speed to every runner leaves isolation unchanged; `Fin.rev` occurs in no Lean file other than the new `LocalityLaws.lean`, so no runner-reflection lemma; the word "mirror" occurs in many `LRC/Spec` modules for the mirror class c to 8 - c and the instant t to P - t, and `lonely_mirror` (`GrandReturnN`, E100) is the time mirror for whole-number readings. (2) `docs/n8/*.md` for "mirror symmetry", "mirror image", "reflect the runners", "determined by ... neighbours", "depends only on ... neighbour": `WN_bsm_full_sweeps_2026_09_12.md` section 1 reports `[VERIFIED - exact]` that the sweeps of the AP respect the mirror s to 9 - s for the pairs r1-r8, r2-r7, r3-r6 (an observation of sweeps, no Lean statement); `FRAMEWORK_COMPILATION_v7.md` and `FULL_SWEEP_v1.md` use the time mirror t to 1 - t; no statement of locality ("determined by the subject and its neighbours") was found. Method limit: text matches on these phrases; a statement in other words would be missed.
**Already proved in the corpus [L] (read at their statements):** `apLaw_end0` and `apLaw_end7` (`Fresh/APLawEnd.lean`, `APLawEnd7.lean`, E567 to E570: an end subject with readings within 1/64 of the AP has as first isolation exactly one of three formulas, 1/(8 x_1) when x_7 <= 7 x_1, (1 + 1/8)/x_3 when x_7 > 7 x_1 and 3 x_5 <= 5 x_3, (3 + 1/8)/x_5 otherwise: the end-runner class rule and the two other landings); `ap_interior_firstIso_max` and `interior_firstIso_max` (`APLawR3_Interior.lean`: interior subject within 1/16, first isolation 1/(8 m), m the least reading); `GridPairLawN` (pair law for grids with a complete residue system).
**Lean [L], new files** (axioms propext, choice, Quot.sound; sorry 0; untagged Props 0; each built with `./check.sh`):
`LonelyRunnerFresh/Fresh/LocalityLaws.lean`: `isolatedAt_shift`, `firstIso_shift` (adding the same speed to every runner changes nothing); `reflectV`, `isolatedAt_reflect`, `firstIso_reflect` (the mirror v i to c - v (7 - i) maps subject k to 7 - k and preserves isolation and first isolation; this is the general statement of what the sweeps of 2026-09-12 observed); `firstIso_unique` (a positive first isolation is unique; FirstIso as defined also holds for a negative instant whenever the positive one is lonely, so locality statements carry 0 < T); `interior_first_iso_nbr` (interior subject within 1/16: first isolation 1/(8 min(|v a - v k|, |v b - v k|)) for its two neighbours a, b) and `interior_local` (two such arrangements with the same two neighbour gaps have the same first isolation); `end0_local` and `end7_local` (end subject, readings within 1/64: the first isolation is a function of the four differences v 1 - v 0, v 3 - v 0, v 5 - v 0, v 7 - v 0, respectively v 7 - v 6, v 7 - v 4, v 7 - v 2, v 7 - v 0).
`LonelyRunnerFresh/Fresh/EndPointComponents.lean`: for the runner with AP speed 1 (index 0), speeds v i within eta <= 1/8960 of i + 1, readings x j = v (j+1) - v 0: `end_window_gen` (from `WindowFirstOrder.window_iff`, E607) and `end0_c1`, `end0_c3`, `end0_c5`, `end0_c7`: inside [c/8 - 1/112, c/8 + 1/112] the runner is isolated at t iff 1/(8 (v 1 - v 0)) <= t <= 7/(8 (v 7 - v 0)) for c = 1; 9/(8 (v 3 - v 0)) <= t <= 15/(8 (v 5 - v 0)) for c = 3; 25/(8 (v 5 - v 0)) <= t <= 15/(8 (v 3 - v 0)) for c = 5; 49/(8 (v 7 - v 0)) <= t <= 7/(8 (v 1 - v 0)) for c = 7. Each window involves two readings besides the subject, so the survival of a point component is decided by three runners (c = 1 and 7: the runners with AP speeds 1, 2, 8; c = 3 and 5: 1, 4, 6). `end0_c1_alive`, `end0_c3_alive`, `end0_c5_alive`, `end0_c7_alive`: the component near c/8 contains an isolated instant iff v 7 - v 0 <= 7 (v 1 - v 0), 3 (v 5 - v 0) <= 5 (v 3 - v 0), 5 (v 3 - v 0) <= 3 (v 5 - v 0), 7 (v 1 - v 0) <= v 7 - v 0 respectively. `end0_pair_law_17` and `end0_pair_law_35`: at least one of the instants {1/8, 7/8} survives and at least one of {3/8, 5/8}, and both survive exactly when v 7 - v 0 = 7 (v 1 - v 0), respectively 3 (v 5 - v 0) = 5 (v 3 - v 0). The readings of the runners with AP speeds 3, 5, 7 (the even readings 2, 4, 6) do not occur in any of these windows.
**Margins checked exactly:** the nearest zone edge that is not the exit or the entry of the component is 1/48 from c/8 for each of c = 1, 3, 5, 7 (an exact computation run in the session; margin delta = 1/56 used, lap bound Z0 = 9, eps <= 1/4480 for the readings, eta <= 1/8960 for the speeds).
**Not done:** the point components of the interior subjects (AP speeds 2, 3, 6, 7) and the interval components, in Lean (the numerical statements are in E609 and E606; `window_iff` applies with their own readings); the mirror of the end-subject pair laws for the runner with AP speed 8 (the mirror lemma and `apLaw_end7` are available, the assembly was not done); every statement holds only inside the radii above (1/64 relative for the end locality, 1/16 for the interior locality, speeds within 1/8960 for the point components); the E609 grid at deviation 1/1000 is NOT covered by the point-component theorems, because 1/1000 is larger than 1/8960.
**Consequence (M7) [L within the stated radii; PARTIAL against the E609 list]:** of the E609 findings these are Lean statements within the stated radii: mirror and shift invariance (all radii), locality of the first isolation of interior and end subjects, the end subject's four point components and its two pair laws (the inertness of the even-distance runners is the fact that they do not appear in any window theorem). The interior subjects' point-component survival and pair law, and the end-subject laws for the runner with AP speed 8, are not proved here.
**Audit:** `rules-auditor` on four drafts: breaches on the earlier ones (rule 13, a corpus claim from five files; rule 18 on the title and Consequence); fixed as stated.

## E614 (2026-10-24): more structure: generic deviations against the grid, jumps and kinks, and the inert even readings
**Map:** owner (2026-10-24): "What else can we tell from the data? ... any non smooth artefacts we can investigate at finer resolution." and "What do you mean the isolation dies? The runner still isolates?" E609, E612, E613.
**What "dies" means [reading of E606 and E609, checked against the map]:** a point component (an isolated lonely instant such as 3/8) dying means that one lonely instant of the runner disappears; the runner still has other lonely instants. In all 52,488 (pattern, subject) cases of the E612 map every runner has a first isolation within (0, 3/2] (the map construction takes the first lonely component of each case and never failed). For an end runner at least one of each pair {1/8, 7/8}, {3/8, 5/8} survives (E613, `end0_pair_law_17`, `end0_pair_law_35`, within eta <= 1/8960); for an interior runner every interval component survives in every pattern of E609 and only point components can die, one of the pair {3/8, 5/8} always surviving (E609, grid at 1/1000).
**Deterministic generic subset [OBS, exact; PARTIAL: a fixed subset, not an enumeration]:** `experiments/n8/generic_deviation_v1.py`: 6,000 deviation vectors defined by a fixed formula, vector j (j = 1..6000), runner i: eps * (((j * P_i) mod 997) - 498)/498 with eps = 1/200 and P = (37, 101, 173, 241, 313, 379, 449, 521), 8 subjects each; every runner has a different magnitude in most vectors. First-isolation classes: end subjects A 12, B 5,997, C 5,991 (12,000 cases); interior subjects A 36, B 35,964 (36,000 cases), C 0. Pair survival counts: end subjects, exactly one of {1/8, 7/8} alive in 11,988 of 12,000 (both in 12) and exactly one of {3/8, 5/8} in 11,988 (both in 12); interior subjects with point components, exactly one of {3/8, 5/8} in 23,976 of 24,000 (both in 24). On the ternary grid of E609 class A and both-alive pairs occur in 1/9 of the cases. Where they occur: by `end0_pair_law_17` (E613) both instants of {1/8, 7/8} are alive exactly when v 7 - v 0 = 7 (v 1 - v 0), one equation on the deviations; by `apLaw_end0` case 1 the first isolation of an end runner is (1/8)/(v 1 - v 0), equal to 1/8 exactly when v 1 - v 0 = 1; by `interior_first_iso_nbr` the first isolation of an interior runner is 1/8 exactly when its smaller neighbour gap is 1 [L within the radii of E613]; so these cases lie on single equations of the deviations, and the 12 and 36 and 24 cases above are the subset's coincidences with those equations.
**Non-smooth behaviour of T at finer resolution [OBS, exact]:** `experiments/n8/nonsmooth_scan_v1.py`: one deviation crosses a wall, lambda = 1/(200 2^k), k = 0, 2, 5, 10, 20 (the smallest is 1/209715200). (1) End subject (AP speed 1), its neighbour (AP speed 2) at 2 + s lambda: T = 3/8 for s = -1 and T = 1/(8 (1 + lambda)) for s = +1 at every k, so T(s = +1) - T(s = -1) = -(2 + 3 lambda)/(8 (1 + lambda)) exactly, which is -403/1608 at k = 0 and -419430403/1677721608 at k = 20, and differs from -1/4 by exactly -lambda/(8 (1 + lambda)) (that is -1/1608 and -1/1677721608): the jump tends to -1/4 and never shrinks. (2) The far end runner (AP speed 8) at 8 + s lambda: T = 1/8 for s = -1 and 3/8 for s = +1 at every k: the jump is exactly 1/4. (3) With the far end offset +1/100 (class 1 dead) the runner with AP speed 6 at 6 + s lambda: T = 3/8 for s = -1 and for s = +1 T = 125000/200001 at k = 0 and 137438953472000000/219902325555200001 at k = 20; these differ from 5/8 by exactly -5/1600008 and -5/1759218604441600008, so the jump from 3/8 is 1/4 minus 5/1600008 at k = 0 and minus 5/1759218604441600008 at k = 20, tending to 1/4. (4) Interior subject (AP speed 4), its left neighbour at 3 + s lambda: T = 1/8 for s = -1 and for s = +1 the difference T(s = +1) - T(s = -1) is 1/319992 at k = 0 and 1/351843720888319992 at k = 20, shrinking by a factor 2 per step (the exact differences at k = 0, 2, 5, 10, 20 are in the script output): T is continuous with a kink. So the first isolation of an end runner is discontinuous at the walls v 2 - v 1 = 1, v 8 - v 1 = 7 (v 2 - v 1), and 3 x_5 = 5 x_3 (jumps tending to the spacing 1/4 of the AP lonely instants c/8: 1/8 to 3/8, 3/8 to 5/8), and that of an interior runner is continuous with kinks where the nearer neighbour gap switches.
**Why the even-distance runners are inert for the end runners [P; Lean support E613]:** the AP lonely instants of an end runner are the points c/8 with c odd; a zone edge at c/8 is (z + 1/8)/p or (z - 1/8)/p = c/8, i.e. 8 z +- 1 = c p; the left side is odd and c is odd, so p is odd. Hence only odd readings p (1, 3, 5, 7) are the exit or entry zones of any component, and deviations of the readings 2, 4, 6 cannot change a component at first order; in the E612 map the six cells (runners 2, 4, 6 on subject 8; runners 3, 5, 7 on subject 1) are the zeros of the whole-set influence matrix. Counts by type: K = 110: 288 births by overlap; K = 80: 1,632 births by overlap (grid 576, other settled 696, swap settled 360); K = 66: 4,036 births by overlap; K = 53: 23,964 births by overlap; K = 49: 43,906 births by overlap and 34,920 exit overtakes (grid settled 432, other residual 23,328, other settled 6,912, swap residual 1,944, swap settled 2,304); in the script's categories the counts of "birth by removing a covering third zone" and "baseline gap, no cover (unexplained)" are 0 (a count of recomputed lines by category, a data classification and not a proof step).
**2. The birth threshold in closed form [P, with an OBS consistency check]:** a birth by overlap is the separation of the exit of zone (reading j, lap n) and the entry of zone (reading j', lap n') whose baseline edges overlap, (8n+1)/(8R_j) greater than (8n'-1)/(8R_j'). With perturbed readings R + δ (δ the signed deviations of the two runners against the subject, in units ε = 1/K), the zones separate iff ε V ≥ -D, where D = (8n'-1) R_j - (8n+1) R_j' (negative at an overlap) and V = (8n'-1) δ_j - (8n+1) δ_j'; this is the rearrangement of (8n+1)(R_j' + δ_j') ≤ (8n'-1)(R_j + δ_j). For the AP wall (reading 2 lap 1, reading 7 lap 4): D = -1 and V = 31 p_3 - 9 p_8 - 22 p_1 with maximum 62, so a birth is possible from ε = 1/62; the landing rule first fails at 1/53 because for the patterns that birth at 1/62 an earlier window is alive and the birth is not the first isolation. Checked: the condition ε V ≥ -D holds in all 1,632 + 4,036 + 23,964 + 288 + 43,906 overlap-birth lines with one left and one right zone (it is the algebra, so this is a consistency check of the recomputation, not an independent test).
**3. Interior runners [L, existing]:** `Fresh.OneMover.ap_interior_firstIso_max` (`Fresh/APLawR3_Interior.lean`, 2026-10-23): for every interior subject (AP speeds 2 to 7) and speeds within 1/16 of the AP, `FirstIso v k (1/(8 m))` with m the nearer neighbour's reading (through `ratio_firstIso`, readings within [m, 7m]), over all t > 0. A birth by overlap of the exit of zone (j, n) and the entry of zone (j', n') has threshold -D/V, D = (8n'-1)R_j - (8n+1)R_j', V = (8n'-1)δ_j - (8n+1)δ_j' (inclusive: at equality a zero-width lonely point is born); an exit overtake of zone A by zone B has threshold from (8n_B+1)(R_A + εδ_A) > (8n_A+1)(R_B + εδ_B) (strict); a component with a multi-zone cluster is dead when some exit-entry pair crosses. Exact result on the five walls that set the group radii (E621): 1/110 (other settled), 1/80 (grid), 1/66 (other residual), 1/53 (the AP) are reproduced as the minimum over the 6,561 patterns, equal to the largest K with a mismatch; for the residual subjects of the one-speed-swap configurations the infimum is 1/50, not attained (the overtake is strict: at ε = 1/50 the two exits tie), so the largest K with a mismatch is 49, as observed. For the AP wall the unconstrained birth reaches V = 62 and the radius is set by requiring the windows at 1/8 and 3/8 dead, which caps V at 53.
**Not done:** the settled subjects of the residual configurations (23,802 certificates, 953 files, running); the closed form checked on one wall per group only, not on every subject; the radii of the certificates are the generated margins (η between 1/61440 and 1/1464 in the grid case), smaller than the E620 radii; the 78 points-only subjects use the pair law, others of other box sizes are untested.
**Consequence (M7) [L, P, OBS]:** in [1..16], every residual subject of a residual configuration has a first isolation certified in Lean at its radius, equal to the largest exit of its first alive component; and the landing rule's radius for a subject is a finite minimum of linear thresholds, reproducing the five observed group radii exactly.

At each one the other readings `x + j s` have the explicit phases `(m + 1/8)(1 + j s/x)`, and the step is a band check of those phases (the `FlankBand` form, E641). No covering and no counting step is used. Whether these openings reach the subjects that the half-step instant does not reach is to be checked by exact loneliness at the named instant.

## E653 (2026-10-30): the cascade's step along an AP block, derived from its largest-exit choice and checked; single-runner perturbations [derived; OBS, exact; PARTIAL: rational sample]

**Map:** E652 item 3 (M3 answer (ii) owed); owner objects: the cascade (in-way readings, largest exit), the other block as an AP; owner: "Yes, perturb them". Shape: a derivation from the cascade's definition, checked by a run (M8); no covering, no count offered as a result.

**1. Derivation [derived from the definition; it is the cascade rewritten in the block's phases, not a new law]:** at the exit `t = (M + 1/8)/x_j` of other-block reading `j`, the block's readings `x_i = x_j + (i−j)s` have phases `M + 1/8 + (i−j)δ` with `δ = s t`. Reading `i` is in the way at `t` iff `frac((i−j)δ) ∈ (3/4, 1)`, and its exit is later than `t` by `(1 − frac((i−j)δ))/x_i`. The cascade moves to the in-way reading with the latest exit (map 11.1). So the step `Δj` along the block is fixed by one number per move, `δ`, the block's phase step at the current exit (with the `x_i` and any in-way own-block reading).
**2. Check [OBS, exact]** (`two_block_step_check_v1.py`, output `.out`): every move from an other-block setter in the gap-strip paths with at least two moves and the nearest reading in the own block: the predicted next setter (block, reading, exit) equals the cascade's in 109,273 of 109,275 moves. The 2 others are exact exit ties (exits 1/7 for runners 2 and 6; 1/4 for runners 1 and 5; `two_block_perturb_step_v1.out` Part A), where the cascade's tie-break (map 11.1) chose the other tied reading.
**3. Single-runner perturbations [OBS, exact; two families only]** (`two_block_perturb_step_v1.py`, Part B): `p = 2, b = 5/12, G = 4`, subject 0 (path through runners 7, 4, 2, all lap 1) and `p = 4, b = 7/3, G = 3`, subject 0 (one move, runner 5): moving one other-block runner by `±1/24` leaves the path unchanged; the landing changes only when the moved runner is the landing setter (`R` 9/5 to 216/119 and 216/121; 27/25 to 216/199 and 72/67). This is rule 3 seen on the path: runners other than the setter do not move the landing while they stay clear there.
**4. Exception status (M3) for E652:** (i) feature: the step differs between families; (ii) what fixes it: `δ = s t` at the current exit, item 1, checked in item 2; (iii) same mechanism: yes, one rule (the largest exit) read in the block's phases. Status: **understood** for moves from an other-block setter in this population. Not covered: moves from own-block setters, the interleaved regime, ties.
**5. Not done:** what fixes `δ` along a path (it changes with `t` at each move); the landing's (reading, lap) as a function of `(p, G, b)` beyond the one family of E652; irrational parameters.
Existence step named (rule 1, displacement frame): none; this is the cascade's own step rule.
**Consequence (M7) [derived and OBS]:** the cascade's move along an AP block is controlled by the block's phase step `δ = s t` at the current exit; the open object for the two-block strip moves from "which reading opens" to how `δ` changes along the path from the bound to the landing.

## E655 (2026-10-30): the quarter-lap landings: the other block on its own grid instant, the own block off it [P for the forced part; OBS, exact; PARTIAL: rational sample]

**Map:** E654 Consequence (owner: "Check quarter-lap link"); owner objects: the grid/residue isolation of E306 (the AP is lonely at `a/8`, `a` odd; a complete residue grid likewise), the cascade's landing, the other block as an AP. Shape: a place (the landing) read against a grid instant; no covering, no count offered as a result.
**Record search (rule 13; PARTIAL: E306 read in full, E654, the scripts named).**
**1. What the definitions force [P]:** at a landing set by other-block reading `j` at lap `M` with `frac(s t*) ∈ {1/4, 3/4}`, each other-block reading has `8 x_i t* = 8M + 1 + 2(i−j)` or `8M + 1 + 6(i−j)`, an odd integer. So the other block is a set of odd multiples of the unit `1/(8t*)`, and `t*` is that grid's class instant: every odd multiple is clear there (residues mod 8 in `{1, 3, 5, 7}`), the E306 grid isolation restricted to the block. ## E674 (2026-10-30): the setter sequence, the cascade's own record [P for items 1 and 3; OBS, exact; PARTIAL: two seeded rational populations]

**Map:** E673 consequence; owner: "Yes, setters" (after: "It does not have exceptions so if there are... you have not"). Owner object: the cascade, from `1/(8 d_min)`, each move to the latest exit among the readings in the way. Shape: the cascade's moves recorded as they are, with no re-ordering of readings; the level picture of E671 to E673 is set aside as a description with cases the cascade does not have.
**Record search (rule 13; PARTIAL: entries of this session only):** E558 (laps kept symbolic), E671 to E673.
**1. The setter [P].** At a move at instant `t`, a reading `d` in the way has signed phase `φ_d = d t − round(d t) ∈ (−1/8, 1/8)` and exits after `(1/8 − φ_d)/d`. The setter is the in-way reading with the greatest `(1/8 − φ_d)/d`; after the move it sits at phase exactly `+1/8`, so it is never in the way at the next move. One rule, no cases: the slowest in-way reading sets the move unless a faster one is far enough behind in phase to exit later.
**2. Run [OBS, exact]** (`setters_v1.py`, output `.out`; populations G, 4,978, and W, 2,900, of E672; reading rank 1 = slowest). Moves per run: G 0 to 14, W 0 to 13 (0 moves: 1,921 and 668). Distinct setter words: G 129, W 380. Setter in the way at the next move: 0 in both (as derived). Setter = slowest in-way reading: G 6,692 of 6,701 moves, W 4,286 of 4,652. Next setter slower or faster than the last: G 3,447 slower, 197 faster; W 1,070 slower, 1,350 faster, so the descending words of G are a feature of that sample (readings in `(1, 8]`), not of the cascade. Ties for the latest exit: W 2 moves, G 0. Same reading sets twice in a run: G 165, W 105.
**3. What fixes a word [P].** Write `n_i` for the setter's lap at move `i`, so `t_i = (n_i + 1/8)/r_{s_i}`. Every condition along the run, "reading `k` is in the way at `t_i`" (`|r_k t_i − m| < 1/8`) and "reading `s_i` exits last", becomes, after multiplying by `r_{s_i} > 0`, a linear inequality in the speeds with integer laps as coefficients. So a run with its setter word and its laps fixed is an open polyhedral cone in speed space; it is scale-invariant without any choice. The ways the cascade finds the isolation are these cones.
**4. Not done:** the laps grow with the speed ratios, so finitely many ways needs the laps kept symbolic (E558's method), giving a family of cones per word; nothing here says the words are finitely many (rule 7: a cap on moves would be a move budget, not claimed); irrational readings; the short windows of E673 restated as setters (which reading's exit opens the window where the fastest reading is clear).
**Consequence (M7) [P for items 1 and 3; OBS for the counts]:** the letters are the setters; a word with its laps is a cone of speeds; the open question is whether the cones, with laps symbolic, fall into finitely many families.

Every chain from 0 stays in the component of 0, so no exit passes the landing `L`. Hence the number of zones the cascade uses is the least number of zones in any chain from 0 to `L`: a property of the zones alone, with no rule for choosing among them.

**1. At a fixed arrangement the landing is forced; the cascade's choice changes only the number of moves [P].** Let `C` be the run of overlapping open zones that contains `t = 0` (every lap-0 zone contains 0), with right end `L`. A walk is any sequence of zones, the first containing 0, each containing the previous one's exit, stopping at an exit that lies in no zone; the cascade is the walk that always takes the latest exit. (a) Every zone of a walk lies in `C`, since each overlaps the one before. (b) Exits strictly increase, since a zone that contains an exit is open and ends after it. (c) If a walk stops at an exit `e`, then `e` lies in no zone, `e > 0`, and `e` is an end point of a zone in `C`, so `e` is not inside `C`; hence `e = L`. (d) If `L` is finite, only finitely many zones meet `[0, L]` (each reading has finitely many laps there), and by (b) no zone repeats, so every walk stops, at `L`. (e) If `C` has no right end, no walk stops. So the landing is the same point for every choice rule, and "the cascade finds an isolation" says the same thing as "some walk stops" and as "every walk stops". The latest-exit rule reaches it with the fewest zones (E682 item 3).
**2. Across arrangements: the record's treatment [L as recorded; read, not rebuilt].**
- Where the lonely set has an interval of positive length, its interior points are strictly clear and stay clear under small changes of the speeds (`DeformationN.lonelyAt_of_close`, E75 item 2): the landing cannot move past that interval. The window fails to be uniform only at lattice points (E296).
- What the record owes is the isolation at a whole-number arrangement, by a direct argument (E296, E384 consequence).
**3. At a whole-number arrangement, the same in the cascade's terms [P].** Take the readings to be whole numbers. Then the zones repeat with period 1 in `t`, and they are symmetric under `t ↦ −t`. **1. One step in residues is in Lean [L as recorded].** At a state `K/(8m)`, reading `x` is in the way iff `|x·K − 8m·z| < m` for some whole `z`, and then opens at `(8z + 1)/(8x)` (`IntegerDisplacementN.inWay_rational_iff`, `nextOpening_rational`, E301); `move_rational_le_iff` gives the move. At the exit of `c`, a reading is clear iff `c ≤ |x(ac + 1) − 8cz|` for every `z` (`clear_at_exit_iff`, E299). For real readings the same in the gate coordinate: with `δ` the signed residue of `ρ R0` modulo 8, the move goes to `R0 + max (1 − δ_e)/ρ_e` over the blocked readings (`RealCase.nextOpening_gate`, `isMove_gate`, log line 12444).
**2. ## E686 (2026-10-30): which of E401's two ways the landing takes: the cofactors' clear set lays the places, the non-multiples choose among them; the way is set by whether a component's left edge is clear for the non-multiples [P for item 1; OBS, exact; PARTIAL: E685's population, readings up to 24]

**1. Derivation [P].** Put `u = 8t`. A multiple `8c` is clear at `t` iff `‖c·u‖ ≥ 1/8`, so the multiples' clear set in `u` is `K_C`, the clear set of the cofactors, of period 1 in `u`, a union of closed intervals. A non-multiple `e` is clear iff `‖e·u/8‖ ≥ 1/8`. By E683 item 1 the landing `u* = 8L` is the first point of `K_C` at which every non-multiple is clear. That first point is either the left end `a` of a component of `K_C` (when every non-multiple is clear at `a`): then a cofactor opens there and the landing is way B, a multiple at the cofactors' edge; or a point inside a component where the last non-multiple in the way leaves: way A, a non-multiple at its reduction point. So the way is fixed by one question asked of the components of `K_C` in order: is the component's left end clear for every non-multiple, or does a non-multiple's exit inside it come first. At a left end `a = (8m + 1)/(8c)` (an exit of cofactor `c`), non-multiple `e` is clear iff `(8m + 1)·e mod 64c` lies in `[8c, 56c]` (the residue form of `clear_at_exit_iff`, E684 item 1). In particular the landing is way B at the first component iff every non-multiple is clear at `u0`, the first point of `K_C`.
**2. Run [OBS, exact]** (`experiments/n8/which_way_v1.py`, output `.out`; E685's population, 218,981 sets; "settled"/"open" as in E685).

- Landing in the first component of `K_C`: settled 43,622 of 83,384; open 63,478 of 135,597.
**3. What it gives.** In this population the cascade at whole-number readings works in two layers. The cofactors (one to four whole numbers, a lower order) lay down `K_C`; the non-multiples are then checked along `K_C` component by component, and the landing is the first point where they are all clear. Way B is a component whose left edge the non-multiples already leave clear; way A is a component the non-multiples enter blocked and leave inside. Which way is a residue question at each component's left edge, asked in order. The landing is past the first component in 39,762 of 83,384 settled and 72,119 of 135,597 open sets, so the order of components matters.
**4. Not done:** a rule from the readings for which component first has a clear point for the non-multiples, which is E401's open step (the non-multiples cannot stay in the partition states over the whole of `K_C`); why there is such a component before `u = 4` (`L ≤ 1/2`), which is the obligation; sets with no multiple of 8 (`K_C` is everything there); irrational readings.

## E687 (2026-10-30): the order in which the cascade meets the cofactors' clear set: shift first, then offset; the mirror pairs the shifts; the late landings carry the reading 1 [P for items 1 and 2; OBS, exact; PARTIAL: E685's population, readings up to 24]

So the components of `K_C` met by the cascade come shift by shift: every component of `K_C` in `[0, 1)` at shift 0, then the same components at shift 1, and so on. The landing is the least pair `(k, τ)`, ordered by `k` first, with `τ ∈ K_C` and every non-multiple clear at `(τ + k)/8`. "Which component first has a clear point" is: the least shift `k` that is free somewhere on `K_C`, and then the least such `τ`.
**2. The mirror pairs the shifts [P].** `u ↦ 8 − u` keeps every reading's clear set and keeps `K_C` (period 1, symmetric), and sends `(k, τ)` to `(7 − k, 1 − τ)` (for `τ > 0`). So shift `k` is free somewhere on `K_C` exactly when shift `7 − k` is; the free shifts come in pairs, and a free shift `k ≥ 4` gives the free shift `7 − k ≤ 3`. Examples: `{1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}`, landing `17/56`, free shifts `{2, 5}`; `{1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 14}`, landing `33/112`, free shifts `{2, 3, 4, 5}`.
**4. Why the reading 1 [P].** At shift 0 (`u ∈ [0, 1)`) the reading 1 sits at `u/8 < 1/8`: it blocks the whole of shift 0, and by the mirror the whole of shift 7, whatever `K_C` is. A reading `e < 8` blocks shift 0 for `τ < 1/e`. So with the reading 1 present the cascade cannot land before shift 1, and a late landing needs shift 1 blocked on all of `K_C` as well.
**5. What it gives.** The question "which component first" splits into "which shift first" and "where in `K_C` at that shift". The shifts come in mirror pairs, at least one pair is free in every set of the run, and the first free shift is 0 or 1 in 218,389 of the 218,981. The late ones carry the reading 1, which closes shift 0 outright. No rule from the readings for which shift is first free is obtained here.

The kind word of a walk is its first link's class pair followed by the kinds of its later links.
- Walks of 3 or more links, heights 16 to 24 in order: 1,814; 2,550; 3,591; 5,162; 6,694; 10,024; 15,486; 21,805; 38,830.

No link has class pair `MM`; no link has lap down or same lap with `b > h`, or lap up with `b < h`.

**2. The lap relation fixes the reading relation [P].** The walk is at `h`'s exit `x = (8n + 1)/(8h)`; the next zone `(b, k)` holds `x` and exits later, `(8k + 1)/(8b) > x`. If `k ≤ n`, the later exit gives `b < h(8k + 1)/(8n + 1) ≤ h`. If `k > n`, `b`'s zone starts before `x`, `(8k − 1)/(8b) < (8n + 1)/(8h)`, so `b > h(8k − 1)/(8n + 1) ≥ h(8n + 7)/(8n + 1) > h`. So each later link is one of three kinds: lap down with a smaller reading, same lap with a smaller reading, lap up with a larger reading.
**3. No link has `D = 0`, and two multiples of 8 link only from height 40 [P].** If two zones share a centre, the smaller reading's zone contains the larger's. A link from `(h, n)` to `(b, k)` with the same centre and `b < h` cannot occur: the point where the cascade chose `h` also lay in `b`'s zone, which exits later, so the cascade would have chosen `b`. With `b > h`, `b`'s zone exits first and does not hold `h`'s exit. So `D ≥ 1` on every link. For two multiples `8p`, `8q`, `D = 8|m·q − n·p| ≥ 8`, and E689's condition `8p + 8q > 8D ≥ 64` needs `p + q ≥ 9`, first possible with readings 32 and 40. So below height 40 there are at most 9 kinds (three class pairs, three relations), and at any height at most 12. Whether the cascade makes an `MM` link from height 40 is not tested.
**4. What it gives.** Every later link of the cascade's walk, at every height, is one of at most twelve kinds, fixed by class pair and lap relation, and on heights 16 to 24 all nine kinds without `MM` occur. The walks' kind words grow because walks get longer and order the kinds in more ways (length-3 words go from 6 to 14), not because new kinds appear. A list of link kinds repeats; a list of walks in this encoding does not, on these heights.
**5. Not done:** which orders of the kinds the cascade can make (a rule for consecutive kinds); `MM` links from height 40; what in the kind word decides the landing's shift (E687); irrational readings.

## E694 (2026-10-30): which link kind follows which: every lap relation can follow every other; what the cascade imposes is that a zone meets only its two neighbours in the walk, `a + b ≤ 8(k·a − m·b)` for zones two apart, with equality where they touch as in the AP [P for item 2; OBS, exact; PARTIAL: E685's population at heights 16 to 24]

**Map:** E693 item 5; owner: "Yes, find it". Owner objects: the zones and their links (E689), the link kinds (E693), the cascade's choice of the latest exit (E682), the AP's chain. Shape: one exact run at every height 16 to 24; one derivation.

- All nine relation pairs occur at every height 16 to 24. At 24: down-down 509, down-same 3,951, down-up 10,310, same-down 1,660, same-same 23,526, same-up 15,292, up-down 20,189, up-same 47,163, up-up 24,885 (147,485 pairs).
- Class triples at 24: `NMN` 60,332, `NNN` 44,071, `MNN` 29,700, `NNM` 11,448, `MNM` 1,934 (first at 24). No `MM` link (E693 item 3).
- Kind pairs whose middle class agrees and with no `MM` link: 45. Occurring: 30 at 16, 34 at 22 and 23, 41 at 24. The four absent at 24 are all `M → N → M`: `MN` down then `NM` down; `MN` same then `NM` down; `MN` up then `NM` down; `MN` up then `NM` same. Not shown impossible.
**2. Zones two apart do not overlap [P].** The cascade chose `h` at `a`'s exit `x1` as the zone holding `x1` with the latest exit. The next zone `(b, k)` exits later than `h`. If it held `x1`, the cascade would have chosen it, or a zone exiting later still, in place of `h`. So it does not hold `x1`; it holds `h`'s exit, which is later, so it starts at or after `x1`: `(8k − 1)/(8b) ≥ (8m + 1)/(8a)`, that is `a + b ≤ 8(k·a − m·b)`. Since exits increase, every zone of the walk meets only the zones just before and after it. In E689's terms: neighbours satisfy `a + b > 8D`, zones two apart satisfy `a + b ≤ 8D'` with `D' = k·a − m·b > 0`. Equality is two zones touching. In the AP chain `1 → 8 → 7`: `(8·1 − 1)·1 = 7 = (8·0 + 1)·7`, so the zone of 7 starts at the exit of the start.
**3. Run on item 2 [OBS, exact].** The condition holds in all 147,485 consecutive pairs at 24 (and in every pair at each height 16 to 23); equality (touching) in 37,741.
**4. What it gives.** No rule on lap relations decides which kind follows which: all nine pairs occur. What is shown the cascade imposes is item 2 (whether it is all, item 5): each zone of the walk overlaps its neighbours and no other zone, so the walk is a chain of zones each meeting only the next. Touching (equality) is where the AP's own chain sits.
**5. Not done:** whether the four absent `M → N → M` kind pairs are possible; whether item 2 with E689's condition on neighbours is all the cascade imposes on a sequence of zones (the converse); irrational readings.
Existence step named (rule 1, displacement frame): none claimed.

**2. The walk stays ahead [P].** Let a chain and the walk leave the same point `x`. After `j` zones, the walk's exit is at least the chain's. For `j = 1` this is the latest-exit choice. If it holds at `j`, the chain's next zone holds the chain's exit `e ≤ e_w` (the walk's) and exits later; if it exits after `e_w`, it starts before `e ≤ e_w` and so holds `e_w`, where the walk's choice exits at least as late. If the block ends both chains, both end at the landing `L` (E695 item 2); the walk's exit after `k_a` zones is at least `L`, and its exits increase to `L`, so again `k_a ≥ k_w`.

Each block starts at a point where the alternative takes a zone that exits earlier than the cascade's (or at the same point, a tie), and it returns to the walk using at least as many zones. In the commonest swap the alternative zone is a narrower zone with the same centre (a larger reading at a higher lap, as 16 on lap 2 inside 8 on lap 1). The family is: the walk, with any block where a not-latest choice still meets only its neighbours and rejoins.

## E699 (2026-10-30): the WBW check in readings and laps: it fails exactly when an extra zone is put between two walk neighbours, passes exactly when the extra zone replaces one walk zone, and a gap of three or more cannot occur; so it is decided by position, not by an inequality on the readings [P for item 1; OBS, exact; PARTIAL: E685's population at heights 16, 20, 24]

**1. The three cases [P].** Let `u = (a, m)` and `v = (b, k)` be walk zones and `y = (c, j)` an off-walk zone, consecutive in a chain (each holds the previous exit with a later exit). Let `g` be the number of walk steps from `u` to `v`.
- `g = 1` (`v = u⁺`, `y` put between walk neighbours): `v` holds `u`'s exit in the walk, so it overlaps `u`, and the check fails every time. In integers the failure is the walk's own link `a + b > 8|m·b − k·a|` (E689). `y` here is a zone holding `u`'s exit, `|c(8m + 1) − 8a·j| < a`, with its exit before `v`'s, `(8j + 1)b < (8k + 1)c`.
- `g = 2` (`y` in place of `u⁺`, E697): `v = u⁺⁺` starts at or after `u`'s exit by E694 on the walk, so the check passes every time.
- `g ≥ 3` cannot occur. `y` holds `u`'s exit, so it exits no later than `u⁺` (latest-exit choice). `v` holds `y`'s exit, so it starts before `u⁺`'s exit. But the walk zone two before `v` is `u⁺` or later, so by E694 on the walk `v` starts at or after `u⁺`'s exit. Contradiction.
**2. Run [OBS, exact]** (`experiments/n8/wbw_v1.py`, output `.out`; the chains of `block_rule_v1.py`).
- Height 16: `g = 1` seen 4,960, fails 4,960; `g = 2` seen 1,027, fails 0; `g ≥ 3` seen 0.
- Height 20: `g = 1` 18,641 and 18,641; `g = 2` 3,257 and 0; `g ≥ 3` 0.
- Height 24: `g = 1` 125,712 and 125,712; `g = 2` 24,827 and 0; `g ≥ 3` 0.
- In every `g = 1` case `y` holds `u`'s exit and exits before `v`, and the walk link inequality holds. The `g = 1` failures equal E698's `WBW` counts at each height.
**3. What it gives.** The WBW check is not an inequality on the readings that sometimes holds and sometimes fails. It fails exactly when the chain adds a zone between two walk neighbours (any zone that holds the earlier one's exit and exits before the later one's), and passes exactly when the added zone replaces a walk zone. A chain cannot jump three or more walk steps through one off-walk zone. So E698's commonest failure removes insertions, and the readings decide nothing further there.
**4. Not done:** the same reading of `BWW`, `BBW`, `WBB`, `BWB` and `BBB`; irrational readings.
Existence step named (rule 1, displacement frame): none claimed.
**Consequence (M7) [P for item 1; OBS for the counts]:** in E698's `WBW` pattern the check fails exactly when an off-walk zone sits between two walk neighbours (125,712 of 125,712 at height 24), passes exactly when it replaces one walk zone (24,827 of 24,827), and a jump of three or more walk steps cannot occur; the pattern is decided by position, not by an inequality on the readings.

## E708 (2026-10-30): when a walk zone sits inside a block: three determinant conditions; it forces the block ahead of the walk at that zone; one instance in 250,502 continuations over five populations [P for items 1 and 2; OBS, exact; PARTIAL: the populations and heights named]

**Map:** E707 item 6; owner: "Yes, find it". Owner objects: E703's continuations, the cascade's walk and its zones, E689's link condition, E694's apart condition. Shape: one derivation; one exact count with the derived conditions checked on every instance.
**Record search (rule 13; PARTIAL):** E689, E694, E696, E701, E703 to E707 and their scripts; no further search this entry.
**1. The conditions [P].** Let a continuation pass `p → c → q` with `p` off the walk, `c = z_k` a walk zone and `q` off the walk. Write `D(z, z') = |m·b − n·a|` for zones `(a, m)`, `(b, n)` (E689). Exits increase along any chain, so a zone overlaps a later one exactly when the later one starts before the earlier ends. The continuation reaches `c` and does not rejoin there exactly when (i) and (ii) hold; it can then go on only if (iii) holds:
- (i) `c` holds `p`'s exit with a later exit: `a_p + a_k > 8·D(p, c)`.
- (ii) the walk's next zone `z_{k+1}` overlaps `p`, so `p, c, z_{k+1}` would be two apart and overlapping: `a_p + a_{k+1} > 8·D(p, z_{k+1})`.
- (iii) some zone `q` holds `c`'s exit with a later exit and does not overlap `p`: `a_q + a_k > 8·D(c, q)` and `a_p + a_q ≤ 8·D(p, q)`.
Condition (ii) is the test in `span_v1.py` for not rejoining, written in E689's form.
**2. The block is ahead at `c` [P].** On the walk, `z_{k−1}` and `z_{k+1}` do not overlap (E694), so `start(z_{k+1}) ≥ end(z_{k−1})`. By (ii), `end(p) > start(z_{k+1})`. So `end(p) > end(z_{k−1})`: the block reaches `c` from a zone whose exit is later than the walk's own zone before `c`. Since the walk takes the latest exit at each step (E696), `end(q) ≤ end(z_{k+1})`; so `q` is not a later walk zone, and, exiting after `c`, not an earlier one: `q` is off the walk.
**3. Count [OBS, exact]** (`experiments/n8/shared_v1.py`, output `.out`). Continuations by number of walk zones passed through without rejoining:
- E685, height 24: 23,674 with none.
- All gcd-1 sets, height 24: 28,036 with none.
- E685, height 26: 38,406 with none.
- Sets containing 1, height 32: 84,062 with none.
- Dense (E707 item 2), height 40: 76,323 with none, 1 with one.
- Totals match E707's span counts. On the one instance, conditions (ii) (determinant and direct form), item 2's inequality and "`p` off the walk" all hold.
**4. The instance.** `(1,14,21,23,24,30,40)` (E707 item 3). In `u = 8t`: `p` = 23 on lap 3, exit `25/23`; `c` = 30 on lap 4; `z_{k+1}` = 14 on lap 2, entry `15/14`; `z_{k−1}` = 24 on lap 3, exit `25/24`; `q` = 21 on lap 3, `(23/21, 25/21)`.
- (ii): `D(p, z_{k+1}) = |3·14 − 2·23| = 4`, `23 + 14 = 37 > 32`. On the walk `D(z_{k−1}, z_{k+1}) = |3·14 − 2·24| = 6`, `24 + 14 = 38 ≤ 48`.
- (iii): `D(p, q) = |3·21 − 3·23| = 6`, `23 + 21 = 44 ≤ 48`; `q` holds `c`'s exit `11/10`; `end(q) = 25/21 < 17/14 = end(z_{k+1})`.
**5. What it gives.** A walk zone inside a block needs the block to be ahead of the walk there (item 2) and to have an off-walk zone ready after it that clears the block's zone two back. Condition (ii) pulls `p` close to `z_{k+1}` (small `D`), and (iii) pushes `q` away from `p` (large `D`). In these populations this happens once. Blocks are therefore almost always single swaps in E697's sense.
**6. Not done:** sets built from conditions (i) to (iii) to see whether two shared zones can occur in one block; a bound on the number of shared zones in one block; irrational readings.
Existence step named (rule 1, displacement frame): none claimed.
**Consequence (M7) [P for items 1 and 2; OBS for the counts]:** a continuation reaches a walk zone `z_k` from an off-walk `p` without rejoining exactly when `z_k` holds `p`'s exit and `p` overlaps `z_{k+1}` (`a_p + a_{k+1} > 8·D(p, z_{k+1})`); it goes on only through an off-walk zone that clears `p`; this forces `end(p) > end(z_{k−1})`; it occurs once in 250,502 continuations over the five populations.

**1. Linearity on the grid [P]** (`experiments/n8/lattice_lemma_v1.py`, output `.out`, sympy). Write each reading `d = 8l − r`, with home lap `l` and residue `r`, and each zone of it as `(d, l + δ)`. Then:
- comparing two zone boundaries `(8m₁ ± 1)/d₁` and `(8m₂ ± 1)/d₂` (cross-multiplied) gives a form whose `l₁l₂` coefficient is 0;
- the point test `(d·u − 8m)·d₀` at `u` = a zone's exit has `l·l₀` coefficient 0, including for a reading at its own zone.
So for fixed residues and offsets `δ`, every condition of the walk and of a chain is a linear inequality in the home laps. Scale enters only through the laps.
**2. Words and their polytopes [P, script-checked]** (`experiments/n8/lattice_v1.py`). A set's word records: the residues of its seven readings; its walk and chain as (reading, `δ`); and, at each walk exit, every reading's nearest-lap offset and side (holder or not). The word's inequalities (`conds`) are exactly the cascade's conditions:
- readings increasing;
- holders `|d·u − 8m| < 1`, non-holders `1 ≤ |d·u − 8m| ≤ 7` on the recorded side, so no other lap holds;
- the next walk zone a holder with the strictly latest exit, and no holder at the landing;
- the chain's links, zones two apart not overlapping, its end, and the walk's next zone holding the chain's previous exit at the shared zone.
So a set with that word has that walk and that chain exactly when its home laps satisfy the inequalities.

Let `R` be a word's rows (`lattice_ineq_v1.system` plus the two rows of the shared-zone condition at the instance's shared zone). Each row `g·(n, x) + h ≥ 0` becomes `g·(n, x) + h + Σ_i min(0, g_i) ≥ 0` over `x = (a, b, c)`. That gives the polytope `Q`: a point `x` of `Q`'s slice at `n` puts `x + [0, 1]³` inside `R`'s slice, so `⌈x⌉` is an integer point of `R`. Where `Q`'s projection on `n` is `[n_cube, ∞)`, every integer `n ≥ ⌈n_cube⌉` has an integer point of `R`.

The real polytope is present from `n ≤ 11/2` in every word; a skeleton first seen at `n = 9` is one whose slice is too thin for an integer point at smaller `n`. For 28 skeletons, persistence at every larger `n` follows from the inequalities with a computed `N`. Under rule 7 the unit-cube step is a counting tool, tagged above. The bound `N` exceeds the observed start in all 28, so it is sufficient, not sharp. This does not bound thresholds across skeletons: a skeleton not yet seen can still have a large threshold, so whether the catalogue closes in this family is not decided.
**5. Not done:** a bound on thresholds over all skeletons (needs the set of skeletons itself, not the 41 seen); a derivation that `R`'s integer points satisfy `conds` (checked only at `n ≤ 7`); persistence for the 13 thin skeletons (for the residue-class ones, substituting the pinned lap and repeating item 3 in the remaining laps); the two `n = 7`-only skeletons; other `d_max`; sets without E710's fixed readings; irrational readings.
